title: "Who is Hiring?" postings stuck near 12-year lows as AI reaches half of all jobs
content:
November 2026 Hacker News Hiring Trends
It's been two and a half years since the last update, so this one covers a lot of ground. As of November 14, November's thread has 244 job postings, down 37% from 387 at the same point last year. Every thread since July has landed between 224 and 255 postings, and August's 224 was the fewest since January 2014. So far 2026 averages 287 postings a month, the lowest yearly average since 2013.
At the same time, AI is now mentioned in more than half of all postings (51.6%), up from 30% two years ago.
AI appears in 51.6% of November's postings, second only to Remote. It crossed 50% for the first time in June 2026. Two years ago it was 30%.
The work itself is shifting toward agents. AI agents (including "agentic") appear in 14.8% of postings, ahead of LLMs at 10.7%. MCP barely existed a year ago (0.3%) and is now in 4.5% of postings, the biggest climb in this month's rankings. Meanwhile, the older machine learning label slipped from 14.8% to 11.5%.
Python (22.1%) and TypeScript (17.6%) still lead, though TypeScript is down from 22.5% a year ago. Rust has climbed to #3, appearing in 8.2% of postings, up from 4.9%, and has been ahead of Go in four of the last five months. C++ and Java are up too, but on small numbers (14 and 11 postings).
Figures in this section are three-month averages, which smooth out month-to-month swings, so they differ a little from the November-only numbers in the chart and tables. Front End has had the steepest fall of any role label: from 27% of postings in early 2022 to 6.6% now, and from 15.6% a year ago. Full Stack (26.2% to 20.1%) and Back End (23.6% to 18.8%) also dropped over the past year, most of it in the last few months.
Seniority mix has been steadier. Senior has stayed around 30% for years, Staff has roughly quadrupled since 2019 to about 12%, and Junior remains rare at around 3%.
Work arrangements have barely moved. Remote is in 55.7% of postings, Onsite 26.2%, and Hybrid 17.2%, all within two points of last November.
New terms this month: AI Agents, LLM, MCP, RAG, LangChain, Anthropic, pgvector, Vector Database, Bun and Deno. Every thread back to 2011 is re-analyzed on each run, so their full history is included.
I also fixed a bug where a few terms with alternate spellings didn't count their own name (for example, "Next.js" was only counted when written "NextJS"). Next.js, NestJS, WebAssembly, Front End and Back End are higher across all months than in earlier posts. The December 2011 thread, which has a single posting, is no longer included.

report.summary: Hacker News job postings have sunk to 12-year lows even as AI appears in more than half of listings, with demand shifting toward agents, MCP and Rust.
report.background: The monthly "Who is Hiring?" threads on Hacker News have run since 2011 and, while unofficial, are closely watched as a real-time barometer of startup and mid-size tech hiring. HN Trends re-parses every thread each run, so shifts in vocabulary double as a map of what companies actually build with. The current slump lands after several years of post-2022 layoffs, tighter venture funding and a broad reallocation of budgets from headcount toward AI infrastructure and tooling. Posting volume has now sat in a narrow 224-255 band every month since July, suggesting a new floor rather than a temporary dip. Meanwhile the composition of the remaining roles has changed fast: AI vocabulary went from a niche tag to a default requirement, and newer terms like agents, MCP and RAG have moved from experimentation to job requirements within roughly a year. Caveat: this is a self-selected, English-language, startup-leaning sample, not official labour statistics.
key_points: Posting volume has plateaued at a low level. November's thread had 244 postings, down 37% year over year, and August's 224 was the fewest since January 2014. With 2026 averaging 287 postings a month, the lowest since 2013, the data points to a structural reset in tech hiring rather than a one-off slowdown.

AI has become table stakes. AI is mentioned in 51.6% of November postings, second only to Remote and up from 30% two years ago, after first crossing 50% in June 2026. The generic "machine learning" label actually fell from 14.8% to 11.5%, so the growth is in applied AI work, not research titles.

The stack is reorganising around agents. AI agents and "agentic" appear in 14.8% of postings, ahead of LLMs at 10.7%, while MCP jumped from 0.3% a year ago to 4.5%, the month's biggest climber. Rust reached third place at 8.2%, ahead of Go in four of the last five months, while TypeScript slipped from 22.5% to 17.6%.

Front-end roles are collapsing fastest. Front End fell from 27% of postings in early 2022 to 6.6%, with Full Stack (26.2% to 20.1%) and Back End (23.6% to 18.8%) also down, most of the drop in recent months. Seniority is steadier: Senior holds near 30%, Staff has roughly quadrupled since 2019 to about 12%, and Junior stays rare at about 3%.

Work arrangements are stable. Remote appears in 55.7% of postings, Onsite 26.2% and Hybrid 17.2%, all within two points of last November, so the return-to-office debate is not visibly reshaping this sample. A methodology fix also raised counts for Next.js, NestJS, WebAssembly and front/back-end labels across all historical months.
report.impact: For the AI industry, the signal is consolidation: AI is no longer a differentiator in job ads but a baseline, and the vocabulary has already moved past "LLM" to agents, MCP and vector databases. That favours candidates who can ship orchestration and retrieval systems over those with generic ML credentials. For developers, the squeeze is real and uneven. Front-end and generalist full-stack openings are thinning, junior roles remain scarce at roughly 3% of postings, and Rust's rise rewards systems-level skills. Expect more competition per role, more emphasis on senior and staff-level scope, and a premium on agent tooling experience. For regular users, fewer openings at startups usually means slower product iteration and more consolidation, while AI features arrive baked into existing products rather than as new standalone startups.
report.tools: To follow this data yourself, HN Trends (hntrends.com) publishes the full term rankings, and the raw threads are reachable via the Hacker News API and Algolia search API for custom analysis. On the technical side, worth watching are the Model Context Protocol SDKs (Anthropic), LangChain and RAG frameworks, pgvector for embedding storage, and the Bun and Deno runtimes, all of which appear as emerging terms in this month's data.
